title: Hindawi 2026.10: the Hindawi programming system for every language and script, on the original Chintamani pipeline
description: Hindawi 2026.10 carries the Hindawi programming system forward from Chintamani's original pipeline: native source, Romenagri, the language's shaili transducers, then the host toolchain, forward and reverse. It holds the language cells for 76 languages across the nine shailis, Grok's tools for ingesting existing code with a dictionary that names identifiers in the language, and a multi-file gcc front end, both put on the original chain. A fundamental regression proves, by execution, that Chintamani's copy is unchanged, every original shaili goes to its host and back, a multi-file project is ingested, compiled with gcc's flags and reversed, and a native name reaches the ELF symbol and returns through Romenagri. Upstream checks bring in SeaBIOS under system QEMU, a Shakti-class RISC-V target and the Linux kernel, pass or fail. BUILD-0102 is kept as received, and every later change is one commit, recorded with its paths and hashes in CHANGE-LOG.md. Chintamani's components keep their GPL-2.0-or-later licence. Version 2026.10.1 adds BURP, the Bidirectional Universal Resource Parser: ingestion of existing projects into any number of languages at once and back exactly, and building them through hindawicc. Version 2026.10.2 adds the sovereign-stack test, VHDL, IDE integrations and the contribution page. Version 2026.10.3 puts the compilation path back on the original pipeline and completes every language cell from its lexicon. Version 2026.10.4 completes Sanskrit, Dari, Pashto, Urdu, Punjabi (Gurmukhi and Shahmukhi), Sindhi, Telugu and Kannada, with 113 GATE programs compiled from each; writes a standard for every language, in Markdown, JSON and Word; lays out the remaining work as packages anyone can take; adds teaching notebooks; and makes one installable command, hindawi, with a manual and a verification guide. Version 2026.10.5 asserts the trademarks, drafts standards for LITD 15 of the Bureau of Indian Standards for the nine complete languages, registers every open task as a work package with the originator's credit, and shows the compilation path stage by stage. Version 2026.10.6 restores and guards the original Hindawi transducer files, corrects lexicon words that held unassigned code points, and adds Parashakti (the sovereign stack on QEMU, SHAKTI included), robot coding for Arduino and ESP32, practice notebooks in ten languages, a local test harness, and the foundation: one normalisation, whole-tree lowering, and readiness and round trip computed from the data; and the explainer site, following one character of any script through the whole computing stack, with the Parashakti, Qwan-tum Tum Tum and AyeKnow posters. Version 2026.10.7 opens the machine in the explainer site: APCISR's original algorithm forming Indic letters on its 9-grid, an 80 x 60 text-mode screen, graphics mode, the framebuffer, the display, GPUs, GPGPU and AI; with AyeCode's alphabets, the products with their release gaps, and Colab links for phones.
